discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated Hubbard-model physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: In 2002 Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a Bose gas held in an optical lattice. This was the first time a strongly correlated many-body phase transition had been realized in a fully controllable, synthetic quantum system. The three then turned the idea into a research programme. Esslinger's group brought fermions into optical lattices, observed Fermi surfaces and realized the fermionic Mott insulator. Greiner and Bloch developed quantum gas microscopes that image single atoms at single lattice sites. These made it possible to measure antiferromagnetic correlations, string order, many-body localization and entanglement directly. Optical lattices are now a central platform for analog quantum simulation, used worldwide to study open problems of condensed-matter physics such as high-temperature superconductivity, and they underpin neutral-atom quantum computing.
